exercise.name: Donkey Calf Raise

reference.title: Donkey Calf Raise
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Calves, equipment Body weight, exercise type Strength

exercise.mechanics: Isolation (ankle plantarflexion, knees straight, hips hinged)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as the heels rise, inhale as they lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s up, 0.8 s pause, 1.8 s down

prescription.progression: Balls of the feet on a step, then single-leg, then a weight belt or a partner on the hips

cues.text: Hands on a bench, hinge at the hips until the back is nearly level; feet hip width under the hips, knees straight but soft.
Breathe out and rise as high as you can onto the balls of the feet.
Pause at the top; back flat, hips stay hinged.
Breathe in and lower the heels slowly to the floor.
Touch down and repeat without bouncing.

mistakes.mistake: Bending the knees to push up
mistakes.fix: Knees stay straight but soft; the ankles do the work.
Hinge from the hips with a flat back; raise the hands on a higher support if the hamstrings are tight.

mistakes.mistake: Rocking the body forward instead of rising
mistakes.fix: Rise straight up over the balls of the feet; the hands only steady you.
Full range with a pause at the top.

kinematics.norm: Full range from heels down to as high as possible (clinical opinion); knee-straight raises bias the gastrocnemius (Kinoshita 2023)
As high as possible each rep (clinical opinion)
Trunk near level, hips flexed about 80-90 degrees (traditional donkey position; clinical opinion)
Straight but not locked, as in the standing training condition of Kinoshita 2023
About 1-2 s up and 2 s down (Kinoshita 2023 used 2 s each way)

sources.title: GymVisual #028412, Donkey Calf Raise, video (movement reference)
Kinoshita, Maeo et al. 2023, triceps surae muscle hypertrophy is greater after standing versus seated calf-raise training (Front Physiol 14:1272106)
Hébert-Losier, Schneiders, García, Sullivan & Simoneau 2012, influence of knee flexion angle and age on triceps surae muscle fatigue during heel raises (J Strength Cond Res 26(11))

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or cramping occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Make sure the bench cannot slide away from the hands.
modify: Tight hamstrings or low back discomfort: hands on a higher support, less hinge.
Achilles pain: smaller range, slower tempo.
regressions: Standing calf raise with hands on a wall.
progressions: Balls of the feet on a step for a deeper stretch.
Weight belt or a partner sitting on the hips.

muscleNotes.calves_r: Straight knees keep the gastrocnemius long and working with the soleus. Standing (knee straight) calf raises grew the gastrocnemius far more than seated raises (9-12% vs about 1-2%) in Kinoshita 2023. The hip hinge itself is not studied there; that it loads the gastrocnemius at a longer length is clinical opinion.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Straight knees keep the gastrocnemius long and working with the soleus. Standing (knee straight) calf raises grew the gastrocnemius far more than seated raises (9-12% vs about 1-2%) in Kinoshita 2023. The hip hinge itself is not studied there; that it loads the gastrocnemius at a longer length is clinical opinion.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Lengthened and holding the hinge with straight knees (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Lengthened and holding the hinge with straight knees (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold a flat back over the hips (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold a flat back over the hips (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Braces the trunk while the hands support part of the body weight (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Keep the elbows straight on the bench (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Keep the elbows straight on the bench (clinical opinion).

phases.label: Rise onto the balls of the feet

guides.label: Heels rise about the balls of the feet
